transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess what finally made me come in is that I’ve been having trouble finishing things I really do mean to finish. Like after audits or mentoring events, I’ll start the follow-up email or a review note or some form, and I think I’ve handled it… but then a few days later I realize the last step never actually got done. It’s embarrassing, because I’m not trying to be careless. I just keep finding these loose ends, and I thought maybe I should ask about it before it becomes more of a problem.
Can you think of any other situations, maybe in your personal life, where you’ve noticed similar problems with finishing tasks or keeping track of things?

Yes… I mean, I wouldn’t say it’s constant, but it does show up outside of work too. I’ll fully intend to do something—like call a junior staff member back, or pay a bill before the late fee hits—and then somehow it just slips past me.

And calendar things, too. Like I’ll agree to help with a mentorship event and I really do mean it, but if I don’t put it in my calendar right then, there’s a decent chance I’ll forget to add it. Which feels silly, because I care about those things. It’s not that I’m ignoring them. I just… don’t always keep hold of that last step, if that makes sense.

Do you find it hard to stay focused during conversations or activities, even when you want to pay attention—like reading something and realizing you didn’t absorb it, or spacing out during a meeting without meaning to?

Yes… I think so. Not all the time, and I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely checked out, because I do try to pay attention.

But in longer client meetings, or even trainings—like we’ve had some AI-tool trainings recently—I’ll start out really engaged, taking it in, following along. Then after a while I realize my mind has sort of slipped off somewhere, even though I’m still looking at the screen and probably look like I’m listening. And then I’ll notice I’ve missed the last few minutes and have to kind of piece it back together.

It’s a little embarrassing to admit, because I do care about the material. It’s not boredom exactly… it just happens.
Have you noticed any situations where you feel particularly restless, have trouble staying still, or act on impulse without thinking it through?

A little, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, but sitting through a long review can feel… physically uncomfortable after a while. Like there’s this pressure building up inside me and I need to move.

Usually I’ll try to make it look reasonable—stand up to go to the printer, get water, or find some excuse to walk for a minute. It’s not that I’m trying to be disruptive. I just feel like I can’t keep sitting still the whole time, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed these kinds of difficulties—like losing focus, forgetting tasks, or feeling restless—in different areas of your life, such as at home, at work, or during social activities?

Yes… I think it’s in more than one area. I wish I could say it was just work stress, but it’s showing up at work and at home.

At work, it’s gotten more noticeable lately. Some mistakes and unfinished follow-up have affected a client review, and… I’m a little worried people are starting to wonder if I can really handle the promotion. I don’t like saying that, but that’s honestly been on my mind.

And at home, my husband has picked up more of the bills and commitments because if I say I’ll take care of something, he can’t always count on me to actually finish it. Not because I don’t care—I do—but I know it’s frustrating for him. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in activities or hobbies that you used to really enjoy?

I don’t think so… not in a big way. I mean, I’m maybe more tired or distracted sometimes, so I don’t always get around to things I like as much as I’d want to. But I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest or that I don’t enjoy them anymore.

If I do something I normally like, I can still enjoy it. Does that make sense?
Looking back, do you remember having similar difficulties with focus, forgetfulness, or restlessness when you were a child—like in school or during activities with friends?

Yes… I think there were signs, looking back. I did well in school overall, so it maybe didn’t seem like a huge problem at the time. But even in elementary school, my report cards would say things like I was bright, but I lost assignments, rushed through little details, talked when I wasn’t supposed to, and needed reminders to finish my work.

My mom still kind of jokes that I could get an A on a test but forget the project that was literally sitting in my backpack. So… yes, I guess it was there, even if it got explained away because my grades were okay. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you were in school, did these difficulties—like losing assignments, not finishing work, or being restless—happen in more than one setting, like both at school and at home or with friends?

Yes, I think so… I mean, I remember it most clearly from school because it was written on report cards—things like, I was bright, but I’d lose assignments, rush through small details, talk out of turn, and need reminders to finish work.

And at home my mom noticed it too. She still jokes that I could ace a test but forget the project that was sitting right in my backpack. So… I guess it wasn’t only one place, even if it didn’t look like a major issue at the time. Does that answer it?
